blocks.text: If f is continuous on \([a,b]\) and differentiable on \((a,b)\), there exists \(c\in(a,b)\) such that \(f\prime(c)=[f(b)-f(a)]/(b-a)\).
An interior tangent is parallel to the chord through the two endpoints.

items.title: Bounds for inverse tangent
question_paragraphs: For \(0<a<b\), prove \(\dfrac{b-a}{1+b^2}<\tan^{-1}b-\tan^{-1}a<\dfrac{b-a}{1+a^2}\). Deduce bounds for \(\tan^{-1}(4/3)\) and \(\tan^{-1}2\).
paragraphs: Apply LMVT to \(f(x)=\tan^{-1}x\): the difference is \((b-a)/(1+c^2)\), with \(a<c<b\). Since the derivative decreases for positive x, it lies strictly between the endpoint derivatives.
items.final_answer: The two inverse tangents lie between the displayed bounds.

textbook_match.note: The notebook includes the extra b=2 deduction; the textbook example includes only b=4/3.

items.title: Exercises: differentiability and missing domain value
question_paragraphs: Can LMVT be applied to (i) \(f(x)=|x|\) on \([-1,1]\), (ii) \(f(x)=x\sin(1/x)\), \(x\ne0\), on \([-1,1]\)?
paragraphs: (i) f is continuous but not differentiable at zero. Its endpoint chord has slope zero, while its derivative is −1 or 1 wherever defined.

(ii) As written f has no value at zero, so the theorem cannot apply on the closed interval. Even if f(0)=0 is added to make it continuous, the derivative at zero would require \(\lim_{h\to0}\sin(1/h)\), which does not exist.
items.final_answer: Neither function satisfies all LMVT hypotheses.
